html:
Hans Egede was a Lutheran minister from Norway who landed in Greenland in 1721 to find the lost Norse colonists and convert them to Protestantism. He found only Inuit, and turned to converting them.

Backed by the king of Denmark-Norway and a trading company, he founded a mission and in 1728 the colony of Godthab, now Nuuk, the capital. He learned Greenlandic and wrote about Inuit life.

A smallpox epidemic in 1733 killed many Inuit and his wife Gertrud, and he returned to Copenhagen in 1736. His mission started Danish rule, which lasted as a colony until 1953 and ended with home rule. Egede's statue in Nuuk has been defaced in protests against colonialism.
sum: Hans Egede was a Lutheran minister from Norway who landed in Greenland in 1721 to find the lost Norse colonists and convert them to Protestantism. He found only Inuit, and turned to converting them.
